The maximal-integral-leaf theorem supplies the second-countable plaque manifold, and the inverse function theorem identifies plaque charts. Fixed endpoints put every homotopy slice in the same leaf. Intervals, squares, singleton leaves and codimension zero are covered. The equivalence-relation operations preserve each slice. An empty connected total space satisfies the neighborhood conclusion vacuously.

Other connected coverings of this manifold are locally path connected and path connected, so the lifting criterion supplies mutually inverse based maps when image subgroups agree. The constructed open Möbius band is the diagonal reflection suspension. Its core leaf is intrinsically R/Z; the cited circle degree isomorphism and lifted endpoint 0→1 identify the core loop as degree one. Its double has degree two, so is not null-homotopic, while its germ is the identity because reflection squares to identity. Reflection differs from identity on every neighborhood of 0, proving the kernel is exactly 2Z, not merely containing it. The natural Mon→Hol projection consequently identifies distinct loop classes; no abstract claim that the two groupoids could not admit some unrelated bijection is needed. The constant loop and double core loop share the same basepoint. Their germs agree by step 1.2, whereas step 1.3 distinguishes their endpoint-fixed leaf-homotopy classes.
